university.name: King's College London
university.summary: A London university founded in 1829, with five campuses across the city and its main base on the Strand. It teaches undergraduate and postgraduate courses, and requires most undergraduate applicants from Pakistan to complete its own International Foundation Programme first.

courses.title: Banking and Finance
courses.overview: A one-year King's Business School Masters on banking and financial markets, for applicants with a quantitative background in finance or economics. Study covers commercial and investment banking, investments, financial statement analysis and financial derivatives, ending in a dissertation.
highlights: Quantitative Methods for Finance and Data Analytics
courses.academic_requirements: A minimum high 2:1 undergraduate Bachelor's (honours) degree with a final mark of at least 65%, in a social science related subject (such as management, economics or finance) or an equivalent overseas qualification. Lower classes or unrelated subjects may be considered with significant relevant work experience or a related graduate qualification.
courses.english_requirements: English language band B: IELTS Academic 7.0 overall, at least 6.5 in each skill. PTE Academic 69 overall, at least 62 in each communicative skill. TOEFL iBT 5 overall, at least 4.5 in each skill (tests from 21 January 2026), or 100 overall with 25 writing and 23 in other skills (earlier tests). Duolingo is not listed.
courses.experience_requirements: Relevant work experience can support an application with a lower degree class or an unrelated degree; the amount is not specified.
courses.pakistan_entry_note: King's international entry requirements page (legacy section of the site): for taught postgraduate courses a four or five year Bachelor's degree with a 70% average is the stated 2:1 equivalent, and 75% for competitive programmes asking for a high 2:1. A three year Bachelor's will usually not be sufficient for direct entry. Current course pages show no country figures, so confirm.
courses.career_notes: The page says the course aims to develop the expertise needed for a broad range of careers in the finance and banking sectors.
courses.notes: Target year fee not yet published: GBP 45,100 is the 2026/27 full-time international fee. International deposit GBP 3,000, non-refundable and credited against tuition. Start month inferred from the 'September to September' wording and from the 2027 intake being the target; module list from https://www.kcl.ac.uk/study/postgraduate-taught/courses/banking-and-finance-msc/teaching-and-modules.

courses.title: International Management
courses.overview: A 12 month King's Business School Masters covering international business strategy, accounting and finance, comparative management and governance, and research skills with business analytics, followed by electives and a research, consulting or internship-based project.
courses.academic_requirements: A minimum high 2:1 undergraduate Bachelor's (honours) degree with a final mark of at least 65%, in any academic subject. Lower classes or unrelated subjects may be considered with a related graduate qualification such as a Masters or PGDip.
courses.english_requirements: English language band B: IELTS Academic 7.0 overall, at least 6.5 in each skill. PTE Academic 69 overall, at least 62 in each communicative skill. TOEFL iBT 5 overall, at least 4.5 in each skill (tests from 21 January 2026), or 100 overall with 25 writing and 23 in other skills (earlier tests). Duolingo is not listed.
courses.pakistan_entry_note: King's international entry requirements page (legacy section of the site): for taught postgraduate courses a four or five year Bachelor's degree with a 70% average is the stated 2:1 equivalent, and 75% for competitive programmes asking for a high 2:1. A three year Bachelor's will usually not be sufficient for direct entry. Current course pages show no country figures, so confirm.
courses.career_notes: The page describes the course as aimed at early-career students heading for fields such as finance, consultancy, healthcare or civic leadership.
courses.notes: Target year fee not yet published: GBP 40,450 is the 2026/27 full-time international fee. Deposit GBP 2,000. Start month is not stated on any page opened, so intake_labels is empty. Module list from https://www.kcl.ac.uk/study/postgraduate-taught/courses/international-management-msc/teaching-and-modules.

courses.title: Artificial Intelligence
courses.overview: A one-year Department of Informatics Masters for graduates with a technical background, covering the foundations of AI, data science and machine learning, reasoning and autonomous agents, and the ethics of AI, finishing with a major project that can be done with an external partner.
highlights: Optional topics such as robotics and planning
courses.academic_requirements: A minimum high 2:1 undergraduate Bachelor's (honours) degree with a final mark of at least 65%, preferably in Computer Science or another quantitative discipline such as Mathematics, Statistics, Physics or Engineering, with grounding in calculus, linear algebra and programming to end of first year BSc Computer Science level.
courses.english_requirements: English language band B: IELTS Academic 7.0 overall, at least 6.5 in each skill. PTE Academic 69 overall, at least 62 in each communicative skill. TOEFL iBT 5 overall, at least 4.5 in each skill (tests from 21 January 2026), or 100 overall with 25 writing and 23 in other skills (earlier tests). Duolingo is not listed.
courses.experience_requirements: Significant relevant work experience may be considered for a lower degree class or an unrelated degree.
courses.pakistan_entry_note: King's international entry requirements page (legacy section of the site): for taught postgraduate courses a four or five year Bachelor's degree with a 70% average is the stated 2:1 equivalent, and 75% for competitive programmes asking for a high 2:1. A three year Bachelor's will usually not be sufficient for direct entry. Current course pages show no country figures, so confirm.
courses.career_notes: The page refers to possible industry work experience and a major project, optionally with an external partner, as preparation for the next career step.
courses.application_deadline_note: Some decisions may not be made until after February and, where possible, by May.
courses.notes: Target year fee not yet published: GBP 40,450 is the 2026/27 full-time international fee. Deposit GBP 2,000. Duration and September start from https://www.kcl.ac.uk/study/postgraduate-taught/courses/artificial-intelligence-msc/teaching-and-modules. The page names only the Individual Project as a required module.

courses.title: Master of Laws
courses.duration_text: Full-time (duration not stated on the pages opened)
courses.overview: A Dickson Poon School of Law Masters with nine specialist pathways, such as competition law, international tax and law and technology, or a general option. Students complete a 45 or 60 credit writing project alongside optional modules.
courses.academic_requirements: A minimum high 2:1 undergraduate Bachelor's (honours) degree with a final mark of at least 65%. A Law degree with an average of at least 65% across all years is preferred, or a degree with at least 70% law content. A 2:1 in Law with at least three years of legal work experience may be considered exceptionally.
courses.english_requirements: English language band B: IELTS Academic 7.0 overall, at least 6.5 in each skill. PTE Academic 69 overall, at least 62 in each communicative skill. TOEFL iBT 5 overall, at least 4.5 in each skill (tests from 21 January 2026), or 100 overall with 25 writing and 23 in other skills (earlier tests). Duolingo is not listed.
courses.experience_requirements: At least three years of legal work experience for exceptional consideration of a 2:1 in Law; references are not required.
courses.pakistan_entry_note: King's international entry requirements page (legacy section of the site): for taught postgraduate courses a four or five year Bachelor's degree with a 70% average is the stated 2:1 equivalent, and 75% for competitive programmes asking for a high 2:1. A three year Bachelor's will usually not be sufficient for direct entry. Current course pages show no country figures, so confirm.
courses.career_notes: The page describes the qualification as internationally recognised and designed to match students' career ambitions; no employers or roles are named.
courses.notes: Target year fee not yet published: GBP 38,300 is the 2026/27 full-time international fee (part-time GBP 19,150 per year). Deposit GBP 2,000. Duration and start month are not stated on any page opened, so duration_months is null and intake_labels is empty.

scholarships.name: King's Business School Global Scholarship
scholarships.provider_name: King's Business School, King's College London
scholarships.value_text: Up to GBP 10,000 off tuition fees
scholarships.summary: A tuition reduction for nationals of countries outside Europe holding an offer on a full-time, in-person postgraduate course at King's Business School. Offer holders who have firmly accepted are considered automatically; there is no separate application.
scholarships.criteria_text: Nationals of countries outside Europe; offer holder on a full-time in-person King's Business School postgraduate course who has firmly accepted. The school particularly welcomes Global South applicants.
scholarships.deadline_note: No deadline listed. The committee meets in April and July; notifications by end of April 2027 (first round) or July 2027 (second round).
scholarships.notes: Pakistan is not named on the page; eligibility is inferred from 'outside Europe' and the page itself says to confirm with the school. Entry year is not stated; 2027 is inferred from the 2027 notification dates.

scholarships.provider_name: King's Business School, King's College London
scholarships.value_text: Up to GBP 10,000 off tuition fees
scholarships.summary: A tuition reduction for offer holders planning a career in finance and economics who hold an offer on one of six listed finance or economics MSc courses at King's Business School. Considered automatically after firm acceptance.
scholarships.criteria_text: Passion for finance and economics; offer for one of six listed finance or economics MSc courses; full-time in-person study; offer firmly accepted.
scholarships.deadline_note: No deadline listed. Committee meets in April and July; notifications by end of April 2027 or July 2027.
scholarships.notes: No nationality restriction is stated. The list of six eligible courses was not captured. Entry year is inferred from the 2027 notification dates.
